html:
In Malagasy tradition the Vazimba were the first people of Madagascar, said to have lived in the central highlands before the ancestors of today's Malagasy. The map uses the name for the island's people in its 600 and 700 snapshots.

Who they really were is still argued. Many scholars think they were early settlers who sailed from island Southeast Asia, part of the Austronesian settlement of Madagascar, and who mixed with newcomers from the East African coast. Others once guessed they were a separate, smaller people, which most now doubt.

Later highland rulers, above all the kings of the Merina kingdom, told of driving the Vazimba out or absorbing them, and some claimed descent from the last Vazimba kings. Their tombs stayed sacred places, and some Vazimba figures are still honoured as spirits.
